suspicion: The bar centres are displaced from their x-axis ticks, so the digitisation or the bar-to-label assignment is wrong.
measured: 8 of 16 bar centres sat 0.0607 pt from their tick while the other 8 sat 0.0011 pt away - an alternating pattern, which is not what a read error looks like.
what_retired_it: Fitting a uniform grid to the 16 bar RIGHT edges gives pitch 12.479997 pt with a max residual of 0.00111 pt, i.e. an exact grid. The bar LEFT edges (pitch 12.481350, residual 0.06942), the minor x ticks (12.480023, 0.06456) and the major x ticks (12.475629, 0.09021) each alternate about that same grid. The alternation is 0.0596 pt = half of 0.1191 pt, which is exactly the difference between the two bar widths the file uses (6.2391 and 6.1200). So the generator snapped some series to a coarser device grid: the panel is quantised, the read is not wrong. CONSEQUENCE: an exact-coincidence criterion was testing a claim the file does not make, and CF was replaced by an absolute nearest-tick criterion with a margin (worst margin 12.3591 pt against a 5.0 pt requirement) while CH now MEASURES the quantisation instead of hiding it. The threshold was not loosened; the claim was corrected.
verdict: RETRACTED - device quantisation, measured and recorded in 05_values_qc.json CH_one_x_grid.

suspicion: The corpus already contains Michael adducts of oleyl acrylamide, i.e. this paper's exact chemistry, so its library may be partly curated already.
measured: A SMARTS probe '[N;!$(N-C=O)]CCC(=O)NCCCCCCCC/C=C\\CCCCCCCC' returned 19 unique corpus SMILES (17 in YX_2026_SDL, 2 in ZH_2023).
what_retired_it: Re-checking each hit by WALKING the chain atom by atom - requiring it to be unbranched, ring-free, all-carbon and terminated by a CH3 - leaves 0 of 19. The SMARTS constrains neither the terminal methyl nor the interior degree, so it matched a C18:1 chain read from the METHYL end into a substituted interior carbon. In YX_2026_SDL's A8+B11+C15+D3 the amide nitrogen carries tert-butyl, not oleyl. STRICT count: 0.
verdict: RETRACTED - 19 false positives of a loose SMARTS. The corpus contains NO Michael adduct of oleyl acrylamide. Recorded in 02_corpus_overlap.json c_substructure_sweep.strict_recheck.

suspicion: This paper's lipidoid labels 1..16 are Anderson/Akinc catalogue amine numbers, so 16 structures could be recovered from AA_2008.
measured: AA_2008 does store a structure for 7 of our 16 tokens (1, 6, 7, 10, 11, 13, 15), which is what makes the idea tempting.
what_retired_it: The catalogue numbers actually in use across AA_2008's 11 tail families are 47 values that are NOT CONTIGUOUS: 1, 6, 7, 10, 11, 13, 15, 17, 20, 21, 22, 24, 25, 26, 28, 31, 32, 33, 34, 36, 38, 60, 61, 62, 63, 64, 70, 75, 76, 77, 79, 80, 81, 82, 86, 87, 90, 91, 93, 94, 95, 96, 98, 99, 100, 103, 109. Nine of this paper's sixteen tokens - 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 14, 16 - are not catalogue numbers at all, while Figure S3 plots a contiguous run 1..16. Under the hypothesis, all 16 would have to be catalogue members.
verdict: RETRACTED, and this is the single most valuable result of the overlap sweep: it closes the one route by which 16 measured values could have been assigned to 16 wrong molecules. Recorded in 02_corpus_overlap.json d2_catalogue_number_DISPROOF; seeded in stage07 as seed_tokens_are_catalogue.

suspicion: AA_2008's N18 family has 44 members but only 43 distinct structures, so one of them is mis-curated.
what_retired_it: This is a KNOWN and accepted corpus condition, not a finding of this curation: CLAUDE.md section 3 records 48 duplicate SMILES groups remaining across KW_2014, BL_2023, AA_2008 and JW_2024, described as head-group collisions repeating across whole tail series, left flagged on purpose. It is in provenance/audit_baseline.json with the reason it is accepted.
verdict: RETRACTED - pre-existing, documented, accepted. Noted only so the 44-vs-43 arithmetic in 02_corpus_overlap.json is not read as a defect.
